summary: Seeking Alpha previews the earnings reports due in the first full week of December 2023 (December 4 to 8), with day-by-day highlights for GitLab, NIO, GameStop, DocuSign, Broadcom and Hello Group. Each preview gives analyst ratings, consensus EPS and revenue estimates and the company's recent beat/miss record, plus lists of other companies reporting that day.
one_line: Seeking Alpha's preview of December 4-8, 2023 earnings, featuring GitLab, NIO, GameStop, DocuSign, Broadcom and Hello Group with consensus estimates and ratings.
key_facts: GitLab (GTLB) reports Q3 results after the close on Monday, December 4; consensus EPS is -$0.01 and revenue $141.04M, and it has beaten EPS and revenue expectations in 8 straight quarters.
Cantor Fitzgerald started coverage of GitLab with an Overweight rating and a $55 price target, while Raymond James rated it Market Perform.
NIO reports Q3 earnings before the bell on Tuesday, December 5; consensus EPS is -$0.23 and revenue $2.66B, and it has missed EPS estimates consistently in the past 8 quarters.
NIO's November deliveries rose 12.6% Y/Y but dipped roughly 1% M/M to 15,959 vehicles; Stone Fox Capital sees potential for the stock, trading below $8, to double to $16.
GameStop (GME) reports Q3 after the close on Wednesday, December 6; consensus EPS is -$0.08 and revenue $1.18B, and the stock rose over 20% in the past 5 days amid meme stock volatility.
Wall Street analysts recommend selling GameStop, while Seeking Alpha's Quant rating says Hold; GameStop beat EPS estimates in only 3 of the past 8 quarters.
DocuSign (DOCU) reports Q3 after the close on Thursday, December 7; it guided Q3 revenue to $687M-$691M and full-year sales to $2.73B-$2.74B, with consensus EPS of $0.63 and revenue of $690.12M.
DocuSign has beaten EPS estimates in 7 of the past 8 quarters and revenue in 100% of those reports; Wall Street rates it Hold while Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating says Buy.
Broadcom (AVGO) reports Q4 after Thursday's close; consensus EPS is $10.96 and revenue $9.28B, and it has beaten estimates in 8 consecutive quarters.
Broadcom shares are up over 67% this year on the AI wave, and it plans to lay off 1,300 California-based VMware employees after completing its VMware acquisition on November 22.

Broadcom is reportedly evaluating strategic alternatives for VMware's End-User Computing and Carbon Black cybersecurity units; Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating moved to Strong Buy from Hold in mid-November.
Hello Group (MOMO) reports Q3 before the open on Friday, December 8; consensus EPS is $0.35 and revenue $413.43M, and it has beaten estimates in 7 of the past 8 quarters.
